newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM BRANDS LABOR'S ATTITUDE TO COLSTON A DISGRACE
The Prime Minister has launched a stinging attack on Labor's handling of the Colston affair, saying if Labor leader Kim Beazley had any leadership, he'd act to negate the Senator's vote.
Independent Senator, Mal Colston, is at the centre of allegations that he fiddled his travel expenses, and is under police investigation.
John Howard says it's a disgrace that the Opposition hasn't matched the Government's pledge to effectively neuter Senator Colston's vote, after the Senator last night voted with Labor.
Mr Howard says Labor covered up when in Government for Senator Colston, who defected from the Labor Party last year.
But Mr Howard says Labor now wants to throw the Senator out of the Upper House without a fair trial.
GOVT: NATIVE TITLE CHANGES WILL EASE MINING NEGOTIATIONS
Federal Resource Minister, Warwick Parer, says the Prime Minister's proposed native title changes will make protracted negotiations like those surrounding the Century Zinc mine a thing of the past.
The billion dollar mine was sealed yesterday after years of negotiations, during which Senator Parer says thousands of jobs were delayed, and badly needed export income was lost.
Senator Parer says such a delay will not be repeated in Australia, thanks to John Howard's 10-point plan.
KERNOT CRITICISES HARRADINE ROLE
Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot says it appears Independent Brian Harradine's commitment to the Senate has diminished, since sharing the balance of power.

The Government, with Senator Harradine's crucial vote, has succeeded in blocking the Opposition's move to have the Senate Privileges Committee investigate whether Mal Colston misled parliament over his wrongful travel claims.
The inquiry's been delayed until the matter's dealt with by Federal Police.
Senator Kernot says Australians shouldn't have to wait years to know the full story, or what role the government played in Mal Colston's election as Senate Deputy President.
KERNOT CONCERNED ABOUT CONFLICT OF INTEREST
Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot says she's concerned about a possible confict of interest over the native title issue, with 29 Coalition MPs and Senators involved in some kind of pastoral activity.
Senator Kernot wants an assurance from the Prime Minister that no Coalition member involved in developing native title policy, will benefit financially.

And of John Howard's 10-point plan for dealing with the High Court's Wik decision, Senator Kernot says she and her Party may endorse some points, but still have serious questions about the proposal to upgrade pastoral land to freehold title.
PM SAYS HE WAS TALKING ABOUT COALITION GOVTS
The Prime Minister has confirmed he was singling out State Coalition Governments when he accused people on "his own side' of unreasonably criticising the Federal Government.
Mr Howard yesterday said he would no longer tolerate gratuitous swipes at the Commonwealth, although he didn't say who had been launching the attacks.
Today, he says he wasn't referring to his own backbench, which he says has been magnificent.
The Prime Minister says State Governments have to understand the Commonwealth has achieved a remarkable degree of reform, and he doesn't accept the pace of change has been too slow.
SHARP TELLS FISHER AND SMITH TO WORK TOGETHER
The Federal Transport Minister says the appointment of Dick Smith to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority is based on merit alone.
John Sharp says he expects CASA's Chairman, Justice Bill Fisher, to put his differences with Mr Smith behind them, and work co-operatively with his new Deputy.
The Opposition says the businessman and aviator's elevation to the CASA Board will be divisive, because Justice Fisher and Mr Smith have clashed in the past.
Mr Smith is one of two new appointments to the CASA Board.
NEW HOTELS TO BE SHELVED AFTER TAX - INDUSTRY
The tourism industry is predicting plans for up to six new hotels for the Sydney CBD will be shelved as a result of the state government's decision to impose a 10-per-cent bed tax.

Tourism Task Force Chairman, John Brown, says two local developers have decided to turn planned hotels into serviced appartments and around four international hotel companies have put their plans on hold.
Mr Brown says the government's decision has come just as hotels are begining to recover from the recent downturn in business.
Meanwhile, the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games has announced a revised budget surplus of nearly 43-million dollars.
FED GOVT TIPS LOWER AIRFARES AFTER AIRPORT SALES
The Federal Transport Minister says the new owners of the Perth, Brisbane and Melbourne airports are committed to lowering aircraft landing charges and making terminals work more effectively.
John Sharp says the sale of long-term leases for the airports, which will put almost three-point-four billion dollars into Federal coffers, will lead to lower airfares.
The Australia Pacific Airports Corporation, comprising AMP and the British Airport Company, has paid one-point-three billion dollars for Melbourne Airport.

A consortium including the Commonwealth Bank and Amsterdam Airport Schipol has paid one-point-four billion dollars for Brisbane Airport, and the Airstralia Development Group has put up 600-million dollars for Perth Airport.
PM SAYS NO NEED FOR ANOTHER MEDIA INQUIRY
The Prime Minister says he doesn't see any need for another public inquiry into Australia's media ownership laws.
Federal Cabinet is today discussing proposals to change the laws, including the scrapping of rules that prevent television station owners also controlling newspapers in the one market.
Mr Howard says he understands the concerns being expressed by Coalition MPs about any decision that would lead to higher concentration of media ownership.

The Democrats are considering pushing for a Senate inquiry into media ownership, but Mr Howard says there've been so many inquiries into the media that most people, except journalists, are sick of them.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
